To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the AVR of the power transformer with OLTC shall be designed in such a manner that it will not change position of OLCT during the critical operation states of HV power system.
it is feasible to control the OLTC position to counteract the power system voltage instability.
1) the voltage instability is a serious problem for power system operators and 2) the OLTC control can be used to counteract the voltage instability.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of an advanced control of OLTC for power transformers to counteract the power system voltage instability.
the design of the AVR for power transformers to improve the stability and robustness of power transmission systems.
the development of a new advanced OLTC control method, which is able to counteract power system voltage instabilities.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

an AVR should be able to distinguish between the voltage changes due to load variations on the LV side of a transformer and the voltage changes due the abnormal operation of the power system (i.e., voltage instability) and should react to the voltage changes on the LV side only.
an AVR shall not change the position of OLTC during critical operation states.
the AVR for power transformer with OLTC shall not react on voltage variations on HV side of the power system, but shall react only to LV side load variations.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the AVR should not react on HV side voltage variations if the voltage is within the deadband and the HV side is in a critical state, and it should not change the OLTC position if the voltage is outside the deadband and HV side is in normal state.
the OLTC control shall be designed to prevent the OLTC from moving during critical states of the power system.
we have developed a new method to control the OLTC in order to prevent voltage instability in the transmission system.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the voltage instability can be counteracted by advanced control of the OLTC.
the OLTC control can counteract the slow power system voltage instability, if properly tuned.
the AVR shall be designed in a way that its control loop will not react on HV side voltage variations.
